stem: When did Mikhail Gorbachev become General Secretary of the Soviet Communist Party?
explanation: Gorbachev emerged as Soviet leader in March 1985.

stem: What did perestroika refer to in Gorbachev’s reform program?

options.text: A policy of restoring Stalin-era controls
Restructuring of the Soviet economy and political system
The creation of the Warsaw Pact

explanation: Perestroika means restructuring and referred to reforming Soviet institutions and the economy.

stem: What did glasnost mean in Gorbachev’s reform vocabulary?

options.text: The dissolution of the United Nations

explanation: Glasnost promoted openness and a wider scope for public discussion.

stem: Which Soviet leader introduced glasnost and perestroika?
explanation: Gorbachev introduced the reform policies after becoming party leader in 1985.

stem: What effect did Gorbachev’s changing policy have on Soviet control in Eastern Europe?

options.text: It reduced the likelihood of Soviet military intervention to preserve communist governments
It brought Soviet troops into every Eastern European capital

explanation: Gorbachev’s decision not to enforce Soviet control helped enable political change across Eastern Europe.

stem: Which statement about Gorbachev’s reforms is accurate?

options.text: They were designed to restore the Russian Empire
They sought to reform the Soviet system but also opened space for challenges to its authority
They established the Commonwealth of Independent States in 1985
They ended the Cold War by a treaty in 1986

explanation: The reforms were intended to renew the system but contributed to political change and weakening central authority.

stem: Which movement challenged communist rule in Poland during the 1980s?
explanation: Solidarity was a Polish trade union and social movement that became a major opposition force.

stem: What did Poland’s 1989 Round Table talks lead to?

options.text: Poland’s membership in the Warsaw Pact for the first time
An agreement for political reform and partially free elections

explanation: The talks between the government and opposition opened a negotiated transition.

stem: Which 1989 event took place in Hungary?

options.text: The country began dismantling border restrictions with Austria

explanation: Hungary’s opening of its border helped East Germans travel west and weakened the Iron Curtain.

stem: Which description best fits the 1989 Velvet Revolution in Czechoslovakia?

options.text: A largely peaceful transition away from communist rule

explanation: Mass demonstrations and political negotiations brought a peaceful transition.

stem: What broad political change took place across much of Eastern Europe in 1989–1990?

options.text: The Warsaw Pact expanded to include Western Europe
All states became part of the Soviet Union
Communist governments fell and competitive elections were introduced

explanation: Many communist regimes fell and new political systems emerged, though national paths differed.

stem: Which statement avoids treating Eastern Europe’s 1989 transitions as identical?

options.text: Every communist government was removed by a Soviet invasion
All transitions occurred on the same date and by the same method
No state held elections until after 2000
Many transitions were largely peaceful, while Romania experienced violent upheaval

explanation: The transitions differed; Romania saw violence unlike several negotiated or largely peaceful changes.

stem: On what date did the Berlin Wall’s crossing points open in 1989?
explanation: East German authorities announced travel changes on 9 November 1989, leading to the opening of crossings.

stem: What event did the opening of the Berlin Wall symbolize?

options.text: The start of the Korean War
The weakening of the division between communist Eastern Europe and the West
The end of the Second World War

explanation: The Wall had symbolized Europe’s Cold War division; its opening marked the rapid erosion of that division.

stem: When was Germany formally reunified?
explanation: East Germany joined the Federal Republic of Germany on 3 October 1990.

stem: What did the “Two Plus Four” talks involve?

options.text: The four Soviet republics and two Baltic states
The two superpowers and four NATO members
The two Koreas and four UN agencies
The two German states and the four Allied powers from the Second World War

explanation: The participants were East and West Germany plus the United States, Soviet Union, Britain and France.

stem: What was the purpose of the 1990 Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany?

options.text: Settle the external aspects of German reunification and restore full German sovereignty
Divide Germany into four new states

explanation: The Two Plus Four treaty settled the international terms of reunification.

stem: Which statement correctly orders the Berlin Wall’s opening and German reunification?

options.text: Germany reunified before the Wall opened
The Wall opened in November 1989; Germany reunified in October 1990
The Wall opened after the Soviet Union dissolved

explanation: The opening preceded reunification by nearly a year.

stem: Which Baltic republic declared restoration of independence in March 1990?
explanation: Lithuania declared restoration of independence on 11 March 1990.

stem: Which three states are the Baltic republics?
explanation: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are the three Baltic states.

stem: What happened to the Baltic states during the Soviet period beginning in 1940?

options.text: The Soviet Union occupied and annexed them, a status the United States did not recognize
They became independent UN trust territories
They were annexed by Germany after 1945

explanation: The U.S. did not recognize the forcible incorporation of the Baltic states into the USSR.

stem: What did Lithuania’s 1990 declaration assert?

options.text: Restoration of Lithuanian independence from Soviet rule

explanation: Lithuania declared restoration of its independence while the Soviet Union still existed.

stem: Which event followed the failed August 1991 coup in Moscow?

options.text: The Soviet Union regained control of all Eastern Europe
Several Soviet republics moved rapidly toward independence
Germany was divided into occupation zones

explanation: The failed coup weakened central authority and accelerated republic independence declarations.

stem: Which statement best distinguishes Soviet republic independence from German reunification?

options.text: Both events created a new single-party federation
German reunification dissolved the Soviet Union by treaty
Soviet republics joined the Federal Republic of Germany
The Soviet republics became separate sovereign states; East Germany joined an existing West German state

explanation: The Soviet republics left a union, while East Germany acceded to the Federal Republic.

stem: Which Soviet republic declared independence on 24 August 1991?
explanation: Ukraine’s parliament declared independence on 24 August 1991.

stem: What did voters in Ukraine support in the 1 December 1991 referendum?

options.text: Confirmation of independence from the Soviet Union

explanation: A large majority supported the declaration of independence in the referendum.

stem: Which former Soviet republic became independent last in 1991?
explanation: Kazakhstan declared independence on 16 December 1991, the last Soviet republic to do so.

stem: Which declaration did Belarus make in August 1991 after the failed Moscow coup?

options.text: It declared independence from the Soviet Union

explanation: Belarus declared independence on 25 August 1991, days after the coup attempt failed.

stem: Which republic declared restoration of independence in April 1991?
explanation: Georgia declared restoration of independence on 9 April 1991.

stem: Which statement describes the Soviet republics in 1991?

options.text: All republics left the Union on one day by a single vote
Republics declared independence at different points as central authority weakened
Only the Baltic republics had constitutional republican status
The republics became provinces of a reunified Germany

explanation: Declarations and referendums took place at different times during the breakdown of central authority.

stem: Against whom was the August 1991 coup attempt directed?
explanation: Hard-line Communist officials detained Gorbachev and tried to halt his reforms.

stem: Who became a prominent opponent of the coup in Moscow?
explanation: Russian president Boris Yeltsin publicly resisted the coup plotters.

stem: What was the outcome of the August 1991 coup attempt?

options.text: It restored one-party rule across Eastern Europe

explanation: The coup collapsed by 21 August 1991.

stem: How did the failed coup affect the Soviet central government?

options.text: It restored the Communist Party’s control over the republics
It weakened Gorbachev’s authority and accelerated the dissolution crisis
It resolved tensions between Gorbachev and Yeltsin

explanation: The coup’s failure strengthened Yeltsin and undermined the union’s central institutions.

stem: Which office did Gorbachev resign from on 25 December 1991?
explanation: Gorbachev announced his resignation as Soviet president on 25 December.

stem: Which sequence is correct?

options.text: Berlin Wall opens → failed coup in 1989
Failed coup in August 1991 → Gorbachev resigns in December 1991

explanation: The coup attempt preceded Gorbachev’s resignation by four months.

stem: Which three republic leaders signed the Belavezha Agreement in December 1991?
explanation: The leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus signed the agreement on 8 December 1991.

stem: What did the Belavezha Agreement proclaim?

options.text: That the Soviet Union had ceased to exist and that a Commonwealth of Independent States would be created
That the Warsaw Pact would be renewed
That the Baltic states would join Russia

explanation: The agreement declared the USSR’s existence ended and established the CIS framework.

stem: When was the Belavezha Agreement signed?
explanation: Russia, Ukraine and Belarus signed it on 8 December 1991.

stem: What was the purpose of the Alma-Ata Declaration of December 1991?

options.text: Restore Soviet rule over the Baltic states
Expand the CIS framework and set out cooperation among former Soviet republics

explanation: At Alma-Ata, additional republics joined the CIS framework and affirmed cooperation among themselves.

stem: Which name was given to the new association formed by former Soviet republics?
explanation: The Commonwealth of Independent States was formed as the USSR broke apart.

stem: Which statement about the CIS is accurate?

options.text: It was a new name for NATO
It was a cooperation framework among some former Soviet republics, not a re-created USSR
It was founded before the Soviet Union

explanation: The CIS linked a number of former Soviet republics after the union dissolved; it was not the USSR under another name.

questionFamily: Dissolution of the USSR and international status
stem: On what date did Gorbachev resign as president of the Soviet Union?
explanation: Gorbachev resigned on 25 December after the union’s authority had largely collapsed.

questionFamily: Dissolution of the USSR and international status
stem: When did the Soviet Union formally dissolve?
explanation: The Soviet of the Republics declared the union ceased to exist on 26 December 1991.

questionFamily: Dissolution of the USSR and international status
stem: Which country continued the Soviet Union’s UN membership after its dissolution?
explanation: The Russian Federation notified the UN that it would continue the USSR’s membership.

questionFamily: Dissolution of the USSR and international status
stem: What did the 1991 UN Yearbook report about the Soviet republics?

options.text: They all voted to restore the Russian Empire
They broke away from the 1922 Union Treaty and declared independence during 1991
They joined the European Union in 1991
They remained under a single Soviet government until 1995

explanation: The republics declared independence and ended the union established by the 1922 treaty.

questionFamily: Dissolution of the USSR and international status
stem: Which event came last in this sequence?

options.text: The Soviet Union’s formal dissolution on 26 December 1991

explanation: The formal dissolution declaration followed the December agreements and Gorbachev’s resignation.

questionFamily: Dissolution of the USSR and international status
stem: Which result changed the political map of Eurasia in 1991?

options.text: The restoration of the Austro-Hungarian Empire
The creation of a single European federation
The emergence of independent states from the former Soviet republics

explanation: The dissolution of the USSR produced multiple independent states across Eurasia.

questionFamily: Yugoslavia breakup, kept distinct from Soviet dissolution
stem: Which two Yugoslav republics declared independence on 25 June 1991?
explanation: Slovenia and Croatia declared independence on 25 June 1991.

questionFamily: Yugoslavia breakup, kept distinct from Soviet dissolution
stem: What happened after Slovenia and Croatia declared independence?

options.text: Armed conflict followed, including a short conflict in Slovenia and a longer war in Croatia
The Soviet Union dissolved that same day

explanation: The breakup led to fighting in Slovenia and Croatia and later to wars elsewhere in the federation.

questionFamily: Yugoslavia breakup, kept distinct from Soviet dissolution
stem: Which pair later became independent amid the breakup of Yugoslavia?
explanation: Bosnia and Herzegovina and Macedonia also declared independence as Yugoslavia broke apart.

questionFamily: Yugoslavia breakup, kept distinct from Soviet dissolution
stem: Which institution was established by the UN Security Council in 1993 to prosecute crimes committed in the former Yugoslavia?

options.text: The European Court of Human Rights
The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia

explanation: Security Council Resolution 827 formally established the ICTY in 1993.

questionFamily: Yugoslavia breakup, kept distinct from Soviet dissolution
stem: Which statement distinguishes the breakup of Yugoslavia from the dissolution of the Soviet Union?

options.text: They were separate federations that broke apart through distinct processes
The USSR was one of Yugoslavia’s six republics
Both ended through the Belavezha Agreement

explanation: Yugoslavia and the USSR were separate multinational federations with different sequences and agreements.

questionFamily: Yugoslavia breakup, kept distinct from Soviet dissolution
stem: What was one early sign that Yugoslavia’s federal unity was breaking down?

options.text: Slovenia and Croatia declared independence in June 1991
The Warsaw Pact was signed in 1955

explanation: The two republics’ declarations of independence challenged the authority of the Yugoslav federation.

stem: Which sequence is in chronological order?

options.text: Germany reunifies → Berlin Wall opens → USSR dissolves → Belavezha Agreement
Belavezha Agreement → Wall opens → Germany reunifies → USSR dissolves
Berlin Wall opens → Germany reunifies → Belavezha Agreement → USSR dissolves
USSR dissolves → Wall opens → Belavezha Agreement → Germany reunifies

explanation: The events occurred in November 1989, October 1990, December 8 1991, and December 26 1991.

stem: Which pair is correctly matched?

options.text: Two Plus Four — founding of the CIS

explanation: Glasnost is commonly translated as openness; perestroika as restructuring.

stem: Which event belonged to the end of the Soviet Union rather than German reunification?

options.text: East Germany joining the Federal Republic

explanation: The Belavezha Agreement concerned the USSR and creation of the CIS framework.

stem: Which statement correctly compares the Soviet and Yugoslav breakups?

options.text: Both ended with a single agreement signed at Alma-Ata
Both involved multinational federations, but the processes and conflicts were distinct
Yugoslavia dissolved before the Berlin Wall was built
The Soviet Union was a Yugoslav-led alliance

explanation: The two breakups were separate historical processes and should not be merged into one chronology.

stem: Which state transition occurred on 3 October 1990?

options.text: East Germany joined the Federal Republic of Germany

explanation: German reunification took effect on 3 October 1990.

stem: What broad map change resulted from the end of the Cold War?

options.text: The United States and Soviet Union became one state
All European borders returned to those of 1914
Germany reunified and the Soviet Union dissolved into independent states

explanation: The period brought German reunification and the emergence of states from the former USSR, among other changes.
